card: Bitcoin Core ignores the addrMe field received in version messages from Tor and I2P peers during local address discovery. Adversarial privacy network peers cannot legitimately observe a node's clearnet IP, but could provide a routable address that the node might subsequently self-advertise alongside its listening port. This closes a fingerprinting vector that could leak custom listening ports and correlate clearnet and privacy network identities. Exploitation requires an outbound connection to an adversarial privacy peer and a non-standard port configuration.
changed_since_previous: The implementation and test coverage remain functionally identical to the previous version.
evidence: PR description: "this fixes a fingerprint which makes it possible to correlate clearnet and privacy network IPs but it requires some not so easy preconditions... h/t to Loupe and instagibbs for finding this fingerprint!"

Commit 533fee6b9d: "if we don't ignore it, we can end up sending them as self advertisement the routable ipv4 address they sent us and our listening port. ignoring it will help prevent our custom clearnet port leaks to privacy networks."
problem: Privacy network peers cannot see a node's clearnet IP, but an adversarial peer can send an arbitrary routable address in addrMe. If the node accepts this address, it may self-advertise the adversary's IP paired with its own listening port, allowing an adversary to correlate a node's clearnet and privacy identities if the node uses a custom or non-default listening port.

risk.why: A mistake could at worst disrupt local address discovery or self-advertisement for privacy network peers, which do not legitimately know clearnet addresses anyway.

summary: Ignores the peer-reported local address (the addrMe field in P2P version messages) when connected through privacy networks such as Tor or I2P. Adds a check in IsPeerAddrLocalGood() to ensure privacy network peers are never considered valid sources for discovering local addresses used in self-advertisement.
